messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: gpu-scaling-alert — GPU queue length on cluster inference-prod-us-west-2 exceeds 95th percentile for 12m; autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes (ASG error). Severity: P1. Incident channel opened. https://ops.redwood.example/incidents/3160001234

Alice (oncall_sre): i'm oncall — seeing sustained queue growth on gpu-inference queue. worker pods Pending due to NoCompatibleNode.

Ben (infra_eng): @Alice can you paste the autoscaler logs? wondering if it's failing on attachrole / launchtemplate mismatch.

Alice (oncall_sre): grabbing logs now. suspicious error: "FailedCreate: launch template version 3 invalid for nodegroup"

Alice (oncall_sre): logs snippet:
```
ClusterAutoscaler: scaleUp-> request for 6 nodes
ASG API: Error: LaunchTemplateVersionNotFound
Detail: LaunchTemplate  lt-0abc1234 version 3 -> not found
```

Carla (runtime_owner): @Ben that echoes a recent rollout where LT v3 was deprecated in the AMI refresh. Autoscaler still references the old version in the nodegroup config.

Ben (infra_eng): ack. looking at the ASG. Confirmed: nodegroup-asg-prod-gpu uses LT v3 which was removed by image-build pipeline during midnight refresh.

Frank (devops): if autoscaler can't create nodes we should manually scale the ASG temporarily to restore capacity. Willing to do a manual set-desired to +8 while we fix template refs.

Alice (oncall_sre): manual scale would help immediate capacity. Any risks? spot/interruptions?

Ben (infra_eng): ASG has mixed instance types and some spot. I'll set desired=8, min=2 max=20 for the group, and use the most recent LT version (v5).

Dan (product_support): Alerting surface: two enterprise customers saw request latency spikes > 10s and 504s on low-priority batch routes. Which customers?

Eva (customer_success): MapleAnalytics reported jobs stuck in queue ~8m ago. I'll message them with a heads-up and mitigation ETA.

Grace (pager): manual scale initiated by @Ben. Kicking off set-desired: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name nodegroup-asg-prod-gpu --desired-capacity 8`

incident-bot: NOTE: manual action recorded. Pager duty incident linked: PD-9876.

Alice (oncall_sre): after manual scaling, still seeing some pods Pending due to node taints: "node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate" — looks like new nodes have a taint from startup script (gpu-init=pending:NoSchedule).

Carla (runtime_owner): that's from init script that marks nodes until nvidia-drivers finish. Could be stuck because driver install is failing on the new AMI for some instance-types. Need to check daemonset logs.

Alice (oncall_sre): daemonset logs (nvidia-installer) show kernel headers mismatch on c7gn instances: `modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia_uvm': Unknown symbol in module`

Ben (infra_eng): can we force new nodes to use instance type g5a.xlarge instead of c7gn? the launch template has overrides. I'll update the LT to prefer g5 series and re-trigger.

Frank (devops): while infra fixes happen, let's drain low-priority jobs onto CPU pool. We can taint a label on GPU node selector to prevent new low-priority pods from scheduling and instead route them to cpu-pool via topology-aware routing.

Alice (oncall_sre): creating rate-limiter rule: throttle new gpu inference requests for non-enterprise keys to 30rps. Applying via gateway rule now.

Dan (product_support): ETA for customer-facing update? we should tell affected customers we're investigating and have a mitigation in place.

Eva (customer_success): sending message to MapleAnalytics: "We're investigating increased job latency caused by GPU capacity; temporary mitigation to throttle low-priority requests and manually add capacity. ETA ~30-45m. We'll follow up with postmortem"

Carla (runtime_owner): infra change: updating launch template instance type preferences + bump LT to v6 that includes kernel header fix. Patching now.

Ben (infra_eng): applied LT v6. Triggering an instance refresh on the ASG to replace problematic instance types. Command: `aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh --auto-scaling-group-name nodegroup-asg-prod-gpu --preferences 'ReplaceInstances:true'`

incident-bot: ASG activity recorded. Instance refresh started.

Alice (oncall_sre): new nodes coming up and nvidia daemonset now completes. New nodes Ready=4. Pending pods reduced by 70%. Queue length trending down.

Grace (pager): monitoring: GPU queue length returned from 1800 -> 320 in 12m after manual scale + LT fix + throttle.

Frank (devops): rolling back manual throttles? recommend keep throttles for another 15m to let the system stabilize.

Dan (product_support): sending update to status page: "Partial degradation for GPU inference in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress; some batch jobs may be delayed. Customers with high priority plans unaffected or minimally impacted."

Eva (customer_success): MapleAnalytics confirmed jobs resumed. appreciates the quick update.

Carla (runtime_owner): root cause hypothesis: image-build pipeline removed an older LT version during AMI rotation; autoscaler/nodegroup config still referenced deprecated LT version. Combined with instance-type kernel-headers mismatch led to driver install failures on some types -> nodes tainted.

Alice (oncall_sre): Current status: capacity restored to acceptable levels, queue draining. Incident downgraded to P2.

Ben (infra_eng): post-incident actions: 1) Lock image-build removal until nodegroup LT refs updated. 2) Add autoscaler validation to prevent referencing non-existent LT versions. 3) Add health-check for nvidia-installer successful load.

Carla (runtime_owner): I'll own the postmortem. Assigning to Carla. Target publish in 48h.

Frank (devops): created follow-up tasks: INFRA-4321 (LT validation), RUNTIME-2109 (driver health-check).

Alice (oncall_sre): final note: if anyone sees queue re-spike, re-open this thread and escalate. Thanks for the quick turn. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed (manual action). Final duration 00:52:39. Postmortem owner: Carla.
